reader.requirement: At --std 85, in a paren-free consecutive sequence of simple or negated simple relation conditions joined by AND/OR, the compiler must accept any relation after the first written with its subject omitted ([NOT] relational-operator object, every 1985 operator including >=, <= and the IS ... THAN OR EQUAL TO spellings), evaluate it as if the last preceding stated subject were inserted (NOT before GREATER/>/LESS/</EQUAL/= is part of the operator, otherwise the logical operator), and refuse an omitted subject that has no preceding stated subject: in the first position, after a complete non-relation simple condition (class, sign, condition-name) or across a parenthesis.

edition-consulted.switches: Edition.Has(2002): at 85 a NOT before a relational operator that is not GREATER/>/LESS/</EQUAL/= is always the logical NOT over the abbreviated relation (§1985:VI.6.3.3 GRL2.2); from 2002 the IS-led form reads NOT as part of the operator
ConstructRegistry abbreviated-not-logical-removed-2002 / abbreviated-not-is-simple-operator-removed-2014: available at 85, refused (COBOL0902) at 2023
<> requires COBOL-2014: refused (COBOL0900) at 85 in an abbreviated relation

reader.edition-search: grep -n 'Edition.Edition|DialectLevel|ConstructRegistry|DialectBehavior' ConditionBinder.cs (BindNegatedAbbreviatedRelation's Has(2002) is the only edition term on the abbreviation path; AbbrevCarry, BindAbbreviatedRelation and BindPrimary's reset have none); grep NegatedAbbreviat in VersionConformancePass.cs
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: only the logical-NOT form (NOT >= c, NOT <= c, NOT IS ...) differs: legal at 85 with NOT as the logical operator, removed from 2002 (COBOL0902 at 2023); the plain subject-omitted form binds and evaluates identically at 85 and 2023

reader.notes: The grammar admits an abbreviated relation only as a succeeding condition after a connective, and AbbrevCarry threads the last stated subject and operator in source order, reset by every complete non-relation simple condition and by a parenthesized group (which gets a fresh carry). All fourteen evaluations match the 1985 expansion, including the five examples printed in the clause. Outside this rule: a literal-only relation (5 = 6) draws only a warning at 85 although §1985:VI.6.3.1.1 says the relation condition must contain a variable; it is the same for an unabbreviated relation.
reader.at-2023: same evaluations; the NOT >= form is refused (COBOL0902)

refuter.evidence: Read §1985:VI.6.3.3 whole. Run E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/sample-shared/out/refute-1985-06/r5a.cob at --std 85, A=5 B=3 C=7: A > 1 AND B < 4 AND > 2 =T and AND > 3 =F (subject is the LAST stated, B); A > 9 OR B = 1 OR = 3 =T; S > "A" AND < "Z" =T; ZERO < A AND < B =T (figurative subject); A + B > C AND < C + 2 =T (arithmetic subject and object); abbreviation inside EVALUATE WHEN and PERFORM UNTIL (A ends 9); A NOT = 1 AND NOT < 2 =T (NOT before < is operator). r5b.cob: an inserted subject whose comparison is illegal (N PIC 9V9 > 1 AND < "X") draws COBOL2532 exactly as the unabbreviated N > "X", so the insertion is checked against the comparison rules. Reading: A > (B + 1) AND < 7 is admitted (=T); I read 'no parentheses are used within such a consecutive sequence' as parentheses grouping conditions, not those inside an arithmetic expression. cite.py: OK  §1985:VI.6.3.3 SR1 ; OK  §1985:VI.6.3.3 SR2.
